english.title: Keep a motor vehicle which does not meet insurance requirements
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), you were the person in whose name a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), was registered under the Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994 when it did not meet the insurance requirements of section 144A of the Road Traffic Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 144A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) Section 144A(2) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that for the purposes of this section a vehicle meets the insurance requirements if -
it is covered by a such a policy of insurance or such a security in respect of third party risks as complies with the requirements of this Part of this Act, AND either of the following conditions is satisfied:-
(a) the policy or security, or the certificate of insurance or security which relates to it, identifies the vehicle by its registration mark as a vehicle which is covered by the policy or security.
(b) the vehicle is covered by the policy or security because, the policy or security covers any vehicle, or any vehicle of a particular description, the owner of which is a person named in the policy or security or in the certificate of insurance or security which relates to it, AND the vehicle is owned by that person.
(ii) For the purposes of this section a vehicle is covered by a policy of insurance or security if the policy of insurance or security is in force in relation to the use of the vehicle.
(iii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - for wording see below.
(iv) This offence was inserted into the Road Traffic Act 1988 by section 22 of the Road Safety Act 2006.
(v) Section 144B of the Road Traffic act 1988 provides exceptions to this offence.
(vi) SI 2019/1047 Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2019 remove the current securities regime, which is used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. Therefore, whilst new securities cannot be issued after the 01/11/2019, the SI provides for a transitional period of up to two years (until 1st November 2021) for existing securities and deposits. This means that new securities may not be issued, however that does not prevent individuals renewing current securities - as long as they are valid until 1st November 2021. After this period (or earlier of the security / deposit holder chooses ) compulsory motor insurance will be required.
